fixes.explanation: Yes, baker, they rejoiced. The text says, "When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army with him, they rejoiced…" (Jeremiah 41:13) Then all the people Ishmael had taken captive at Mizpah turned and went over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14). I bet they were glad to see him.

Right, baker, the number is eight. "…Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and went to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:15) He came to Mizpah with ten men (Jeremiah 41:1), so ten isn't the number here. The captives had turned and gone over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14).

Yes, baker, that's the reason. "…they were afraid of the Chaldeans because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land." (Jeremiah 41:18) Ishmael did the killing, and the people were the ones who felt the fear. They wanted to escape the Chaldeans.
